newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES UP TO $853.7 MLN IN MARCH.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA C.BANK RESERVES UP TO $853.7 MLN IN MARCH.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Thursday its total foreign exchange reserves rose to $853.7 million in March from $697.7 million at end-February.
Local bankers said the recovery followed the BNR's interventions on the foreign exchange market to buy dollars to prevent a sharper appreciation of the national leu currency.

Tough monetary policies led deposit rates higher in March helping the leu to firm at about 6,800 to the dollar after sinking to 9,000 in mid-February. One-month deposit rates are now at an annual 150 percent, compared to 50 in the New Year.
BNR data also showed foreign reserve assets in the banking system were almost flat at $2.76 billion in February from $2.77 billion the previous month. March figures were not available.
End-February reserve assets include gold reserves of about 88 tonnes, Special Drawing Rights and the hard currency reserves of local banks and of the BNR.
Romania's external debt servicing is estimated at some $1.5 billion in 1997, when the Balkan country is entitled to borrow up to $3.2 billion from international capital markets.
